canonical_question: How does setting the indenter speed to 10 m/s affect the comparison between simulation strain rates and experimental wear rates?

question_variants.question: How does setting the indenter speed to 10 m/s affect the comparison between simulation strain rates and experimental wear rates?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper specifies the indenter speed (10 m/s) but does not provide an analysis or discussion on how this speed affects the comparison between simulation strain rates and experimental wear rates.

answers.answer: The text states the speed used but does not discuss its implications for comparing simulation strain rates to experimental wear rates.
answers.material: Cu matrix / FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating
answers.measurement_outcome: pressed into the matrix at a speed of 10 m/s along the negative direction of the Z axis
answers.boundary_limitation: No comparison to experimental wear rates or strain rate analysis provided
evidence_spans: In the nanoindentation model, single crystal Cu was used as the matrix material and FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy was used as the coating material.
The same lattice types of both materials were set.
The model size of the Cu matrix was 100 Å × 100 Å × 55 Å, and the total number of atoms was 47,111.
